verdict.rationale: Connecting a Kubernetes cluster, including one behind a firewall or NAT, is a fair question for a CI/CD-bearing developer platform, so the axis applies. The pack only offers generic CI/CD and Actions claims ("Ship faster with secure, reliable CI/CD") and a community wish for self-hosted runners; neither documents a Kubernetes cluster connection, firewall/NAT agent connectivity, or cluster monitoring. These are adjacent at most and earn no credit.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can connect a Kubernetes cluster, including one behind a firewall or NAT, to deploy and monitor applications
